creditRule: A defect is implemented only with a traceable code change that passed focused inspection and focused tests. Citation of an id by tooling or by a register-derived builder is not evidence. Qualification (typecheck, full suites, build, CI, runtime) is a separate pending dimension.

DEF-0C1-REV-ADVERSE-PARTY-IDS-ARE-CHECKE.explanation: requireAdverseMembers checks every named adverse party is an active member of the organization (one generic refusal, no per-identity oracle) before anything is written. Real-SQL pglite test.

DEF-0C1-REV-POST-HAS-NO-RATE-LIMIT-OR-ID.explanation: Per-member intake is serialised with an advisory lock; a repeat of an identical open review returns that review (200, alreadyOpen) instead of another append-only row; a daily cap of 10 raises REVIEW_INTAKE_LIMIT answered 429 with Retry-After. pglite and route tests.

DEF-0C1-REV-POST-READS-AN-UNCAPPED-REQUE.explanation: readBoundedBody enforces a 2 KiB cap by declared length and by streamed length, cancelling the stream, before JSON parsing; 413 otherwise.

DEF-0C1-REV-THE-ROUTE-RESOLVES-ITS-ORGAN.explanation: Both handlers call withRLSContext({ organizationId }) with the organization the route resolved, so the database context cannot be a second resolution.

DEF-0C1-REV-FAILURES-OUTSIDE-THE-STORE-A.explanation: reviewErrorResponse maps ApiError to 401/403 and logs any other failure with logger.error, answering a structured INTERNAL_ERROR 500 that does not echo the cause.

DEF-0C1-REV-THE-OVERSIGHT-LIST-RETURNS-C.explanation: An oversight read persists review.oversight.read with the disclosed review ids and the privileged count through persistAtomicAudit in the same transaction; an own-only list records nothing.

DEF-0B9-MOB-NOTIFICATION-READS-ANSWER-20.explanation: The swallowing try/catch is removed from the list and count reads, so a failed read is a failure; page and limit are parsed strictly (400).

DEF-0B9-MOB-STEWARD-NOTIFICATION-IS-STOR.explanation: Strict schema bounds title, message, type, label, link (same-site path only) and data size and requires a future expiry; the author is stored in data.origin (client origin overwritten); 100 per hour per steward; the audit carries a content digest.

DEF-0B9-MOB-NOTIFICATION-PATCH-READ-FLAG.explanation: Only a real boolean is accepted; readAt is set when read and cleared when unread; the audit stores a boolean.

DEF-0B9-MOB-NOTIFICATION-TEST-ROUTE-EXER.explanation: The route states it tests the inbox only, reports each channel's real state, reuses a recent unread test row, and expires new rows after an hour.

DEF-0B9-MOB-PUSH-DEVICE-REGISTRATION-REQ.explanation: The person who holds the phone registers it at the member floor, every row is the caller's own, and the token is never returned (batch B02).

DEF-0B9-MOB-TWO-DEVICE-TABLES-NO-ROUTE-R.explanation: Both device tables now have an owner removal route (PATCH preferences and DELETE for push devices, DELETE for mobile devices), audited.
DEF-0B9-MOB-TWO-DEVICE-TABLES-NO-ROUTE-R.remaining: The two tables are not consolidated, and no sender reads either table (services/fcm-service.ts and lib/mobile/mobile-engine.ts remain unimported by any route or worker).

DEF-0B9-MOB-DEVICE-ROWS-ARE-RETURNED-WHO.explanation: omitFromResponse removes the push token from every push-device response; the sync route projects an explicit safe column list that excludes the token, the jailbreak flag and the compliance columns.

DEF-0B9-MOB-SYNC-PATH-REGISTERS-A-DEVICE.explanation: The route accepts the body its only caller sends (a browser needs no token), says in every response that no synchronization was performed, and the Sync now button shows success only when the response says it synced.
DEF-0B9-MOB-SYNC-PATH-REGISTERS-A-DEVICE.remaining: No synchronization is implemented: mobile_sync_queue is still never read or written.

DEF-0B9-MOB-DEVICE-REREGISTRATION-KEEPS-.explanation: Re-registration updates organizationId, a token held by another device is a 409, and every field is length-validated against its column before any write.

DEF-0B9-MOB-PUSH-SUBSCRIBE-AND-UNSUBSCRI.explanation: Web push subscription has no store and no sender, so both routes answer 501 and read or write nothing, instead of CRUD over the campaign table that failed and left the client believing it had subscribed.

DEF-0B9-MOB-PUSH-CAMPAIGN-ROWS-ARE-READA.explanation: The only paths that served push_notifications to a member are removed; the table is no longer classified for generic CRUD, so it is DENIED by default.

DEF-0B9-MOB-PUSH-CAMPAIGN-CREATE-ACCEPTS.explanation: No route can create a push_notifications row any more, so a row cannot be written as sent with delivery counters.

DEF-0B9-MOB-MOBILE-NOTIFICATIONS-PATH-SE.explanation: The mobile path runs the same handlers as /api/notifications (shared in lib/notifications/inbox-handlers.ts, each path behind its own visible guard), so it serves the in-app inbox (own rows) instead of the scheduled queue table.

DEF-0B9-MOB-MOBILE-NOTIFICATIONS-CREATE-.explanation: Create now goes through the inbox POST, which checks the recipient is a member of the organization, validates input and cannot set a sent state; the scheduled-queue table has no generic route.

DEF-0B9-MOB-NEGOTIATIONS-PATH-REPEATS-TH.explanation: Both paths take their read floor and writable fields from one shared rules module, so a restriction cannot be added to one path and missed on the other.

DEF-0B9-MOB-NEGOTIATION-CREATE-LETS-A-ST.explanation: writableFields excludes strike-vote, mandate, cost, status, confidentiality and agreement-link fields on create and update (400), and negotiations are read at steward level instead of member.

DEF-0B9-MOB-MEETING-ROOM-BOOKING-RULES-A.explanation: Platform 0041 evolves the room_bookings stub to its 26 missing declared columns, cache 0035 forces row-level security by organization, and the manifest reclassifies the table from LATENT_UNREACHABLE to TENANT_RLS_REQUIRED with SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE only. POST /api/meeting-rooms/[id]/bookings now accepts a booking only when evaluateBooking allows it (hours, blocked dates, duration, how far ahead, who may book, capacity, approval); a room needing approval holds the slot as scheduled until staff other than the booker confirm it. Proved against real SQL on PGlite, including the room-locking trigger. Not applied to a native database. The unused calendar-service placeholders (listMeetingRooms returned an empty list, checkRoomAvailability always answered available, bookMeetingRoom returned a generated id without storing anything, cancelRoomBooking reported success) were removed together with their four stub tests (disclosed); overlap is refused by a trigger that locks the room row (SQLSTATE 23P01, answered as 409).

DEF-0B9-MOB-MEETING-ROOM-BOOKINGS-PATH-P.explanation: The bookings path no longer edits the room row or exports PATCH or any room CRUD; it answers 501 for every method and reads or writes nothing.

DEF-0B6-SYS-CRON-GET-ALIASES-RUN-STATE-C.explanation: All four aliases export POST only; so do the other ten scheduled routes (codemod f01-cron-post-only.cjs, idempotent). A contract test fails if any manifest route exports a method other than POST.

DEF-0B6-SYS-CRON-ROUTES-HAVE-NO-SCHEDULE.explanation: The manifest declares all 18 scheduled routes; apps.bicep generates one Container Apps schedule job per entry (POST with the cron secret, curl -f so a non-2xx fails the run). Compiles with az bicep; the contract test fails when a cron route is missing from the manifest or the bicep stops reading it.

DEF-0B6-SYS-CRON-EDGE-SECRET-CHECK-DIFFE.explanation: One shared rule (x-cron-secret or bearer; CRON_SECRET_KEY then CRON_SECRET; unset never matches) used by withApi, verifyCronAuth, the rewards route and the edge check, which now compares in constant time over SHA-256 digests via WebCrypto (edge-safe) instead of !==. CRON_API_ROUTES is derived from the manifest.

DEF-0B6-SYS-CALENDAR-SYNC-SCHEDULE-ENTRY.explanation: The vercel.json entry (no method, no secret) is removed; calendar-sync is scheduled as a POST Container Apps job every 15 minutes, and verifyCronAuth now accepts the secret as a bearer token as well as x-cron-secret.

DEF-0B6-SYS-LOCATION-RETENTION-HAS-NO-SC.explanation: location-retention is an hourly POST Container Apps job generated from the manifest.

DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-ACCEPTS-THE-SE.explanation: The route's own Authorization-only CRON_SECRET-only check is replaced by the shared rule, so one transport (x-cron-secret) satisfies the edge and the route; the edge compare is constant time; the GET handler is removed.

DEF-0B6-SYS-PER-CAPITA-CRON-REPORTS-SUCC.explanation: The calculation catch now records, logs and returns the failing organization; the save step returns the failing organization ids; the route answers 500 with counts and ids through jobResponse when any failed, and no longer runs markOverdueRemittances a second time.

DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-REPORTS-SUCCES.explanation: An unknown task is a 400 that runs nothing; a rejected organization, an organization that resolves with success false, and an expiration batch whose own flag is false are failures; the run answers 500 naming the scopes; rejected errors serialise as text instead of {}.

DEF-0B6-SYS-EXTERNAL-DATA-SYNC-FAILURES-.explanation: The handler answers 500 for a run with any failed source and for the outer failure; every sync method writes the log row through syncLogOutcome: partial (not completed) when records failed, with the bounded collected error list in error_details.

DEF-0B1-BILLING-SCHEDULER-LATENT.explanation: billing-lifecycle is now a daily POST schedule job.
DEF-0B1-BILLING-SCHEDULER-LATENT.remaining: The route's generator still needs a session, so it cannot run headless; that needs its own review.

DEF-0B6-EDU-CRON-REPORTS-SUCCESS-AFTER-F.explanation: A run with failed session-reminder or expiry-warning sends answers 500 through jobResponse naming the failed batch, with the sent/failed counts and collected errors in the body; the message no longer claims success. The route writes nothing, so it is classified as a read-only POST for the audit ratchet.

DEF-0B6-SYS-RESEND-UNMATCHED-EVENTS-ACKN.explanation: An event matching neither a message_log row nor a delivery-ledger row answers 404 retryable so the provider redelivers (covering an event that beats the sender storing the provider message id); a redelivery after the row exists applies it. Both are tested against PostgreSQL (pglite).

DEF-0B6-SYS-RESEND-STATUS-OVERWRITTEN-BY.explanation: Status only advances to a higher rank (a late sent, delivered or opened never overwrites bounced, failed or complained); fact timestamps are filled when missing; existing metadata is preserved. The table comment no longer claims the log is immutable and states the real rule. Mutation-proved.

DEF-0B6-SYS-RESEND-REDELIVERY-DOUBLE-COU.explanation: Each statistic counts a message at most once (a counted set persisted in message_log.metadata, seeded from timestamps and terminal status for older rows), and the campaign counters advance inside the UPDATE (jsonb || jsonb_build_object over the stored value) rather than from a value read earlier. Tested with redelivery and with a counter another writer already advanced. Mutation-proved.

DEF-0B6-SYS-RESEND-SUPPRESSION-UPDATES-O.explanation: A complaint or suppression now creates the preference row when none exists, writes a revoked consent record and the audit entry, and applies once per message in the same transaction.
DEF-0B6-SYS-RESEND-SUPPRESSION-UPDATES-O.remaining: Suppression is still scoped to the one organization on the message row; suppressing the same address in other organizations and in distribution-list subscriptions needs a cross-organization address-suppression design.

DEF-0B6-SYS-RESEND-LEDGER-CALLBACK-OUTSI.explanation: recordProviderCallback takes the caller's transaction (inserting inside a savepoint so a duplicate does not abort it); the webhook runs it in the same transaction as the message row, so a ledger failure rolls everything back and the retry repeats nothing. An unmatched or ambiguous ledger result is logged, and an event matching nothing is retried. Rollback proved with a failing audit write.

DEF-0B6-SYS-RESEND-MESSAGE-ID-LOOKUP-UNI.explanation: Migration 20261031 creates a unique (provider, provider_message_id) index when no pair repeats, otherwise a plain index with the duplicate count reported; both branches and idempotence executed on PostgreSQL (pglite). The webhook locks the row (FOR UPDATE) and refuses with 409 when two rows carry the id. Native PostgreSQL qualification of the migration is still to run.

DEF-0B8-ICRA-SHOPIFY-DISCOUNT-CODE-NEVER.explanation: The code issued and the code parsed are defined together (shopify-redemption-rules): UE plus the 32 hex characters of the redemption id, lossless. The parser also accepts the dashed form and resolves a legacy 12-character code only as a prefix inside the shop's organization among redemptions awaiting payment, and only when exactly one matches, so codes already issued still complete. Round trip unit-tested; the full paid, fulfilled, refunded lifecycle runs against PostgreSQL (pglite).

DEF-0B8-ICRA-SHOPIFY-WEBHOOK-ACKNOWLEDGE.explanation: A failure answers 500; an event that cannot be applied yet (a fulfilment or refund for an order not recorded as paid) answers 503 with Retry-After; neither records a receipt, so the redelivery is applied. A receipt is recorded only after the handler, only for a final outcome, and tolerates a concurrent duplicate. The handlers are idempotent on their own state (an order already applied is a success), so the separate receipt transaction cannot lose or double-apply an event. Mutation-proved.

DEF-0B8-ICRA-SHOPIFY-ANY-REFUND-EVENT-RE.explanation: A refund returns its share of the credits (floor of creditsSpent x refunded line-item subtotal / order line-item total), a later refund returns its own share, each Shopify refund id is applied once, the redemption becomes refunded only when everything spent has come back, and the total returned never exceeds the credits spent. Refunds are recorded in the stored payload and in the audit entry. Mutation-proved.

DEF-0B8-ICRA-SHOPIFY-WEBHOOK-STORES-FULL.explanation: The receipt keeps only the topic, shop domain and the order or refund id; the redemption keeps order facts (number, currency, totals, product and variant ids, quantity, price) and no customer id, e-mail, name or line-item title; discount codes are no longer logged. Migration 20261102 irreversibly redacts what was already stored in webhook_receipts and reward_redemptions (executed on PostgreSQL pglite, repeatable).

DEF-0B8-ICRA-SHOPIFY-WEBHOOK-QUERIES-TEN.explanation: Every lookup and write of the handler runs inside withRLSContext bound to the shop's organization, and the redemption's organization is checked against it. The organization comes from the shop domain through migration 20261101: a unique index on the lower-cased domain and a column-level SELECT (org_id, shop_domain) grant with a read-only policy for the system role; the token and secret references stay unreadable (executed with real roles and RLS on pglite). The runtime-role behaviour under the real application roles is still to be qualified on native PostgreSQL.

DEF-0B8-ICRA-SHOPIFY-SHOP-DOMAIN-NEVER-C.explanation: The shop domain header must belong to exactly one organization or the signed event is refused (403, logged), each shop has its own rate-limit allowance, and the pre-signature limit is keyed on one normalised address instead of the whole forwarded-for string.
DEF-0B8-ICRA-SHOPIFY-SHOP-DOMAIN-NEVER-C.remaining: The HMAC still uses one global SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET for every organization; per-organization secrets (shopify_config.webhook_secret_ref) need the secret store. The address key is only as trustworthy as the front proxy that sets the header.

DEF-0B6-SYS-SLA-WATCHDOG-EVENTS-HAVE-NO-.explanation: The in-process bus events are replaced by a durable inbox alert for the steward each late or at-risk claim is assigned to, written inside that organization's own context and deduplicated by a unique index over (organization, user, claim+kind+deadline) from migration 20261103: a rerun, retry or overlapping run adds nothing; a new deadline or escalation alerts again. Unassigned claims are counted in the result. Real-SQL tested; mutation-proved (dedupe, recipient). Native PostgreSQL qualification of the migration is still to run.

DEF-0B6-SYS-SLA-WATCHDOG-UNBOUNDED-SCAN-.explanation: The watchdog keyset-pages the claims scan under a page cap, assesses each claim once, awaits the metric writes keyed by organization and hour, and reports a failed metric or alert write as a failed job (existing implementation, existing route and pglite tests).

DEF-0B3-ALERT-SWEEP-AUDIT-ATOMICITY-UNPR.explanation: The rule, inbox notices, execution record and audit entry are all written on the sweep's transaction handle in one savepoint per signal (the module-level db handle is no longer used for writes). Proved on PostgreSQL: an audit failure leaves no inbox row and no execution for that alert while other organizations' alerts are kept, and the next run completes it.

DEF-0B6-SYS-OBSERVABILITY-SWEEP-RECORDS-.explanation: The never-read pending notification_tracking row is no longer written and an execution records only the channel that delivered (in_app, with the recipient count) and its measured time. The alert goes to the organization's active administrators and president; an alert nobody can receive is a failed execution and a failed job (500), not a success. Reruns in the same hour alert nobody twice. No e-mail is sent or claimed; delivering alerts by e-mail is not part of this fix.

DEF-0B6-SYS-CALENDAR-SYNC-FIRST-PAGE-ONL.explanation: The Google import follows every page (250 per call, 50-page bound that fails instead of truncating), the cron passes the stored sync token (without the window and ordering Google rejects with one), a 410 falls back to a full sync, and the new token is stored only when every page was read and every event applied; otherwise the import throws and the connection is recorded as failed with a retry time. Per-event and token-store errors are no longer swallowed. The due connections are locked FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and leased for 15 minutes in the same transaction, each lease bound to the row's organization. Google only: the Microsoft import has the same shape and is not yet changed.

DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-ANNIVERSARY-AW.explanation: Repeat protection (an advisory lock per organization and award type, and a same-day NOT EXISTS over the member's awards in any state) was already in the source and is proven on PostgreSQL by anniversary-idempotency.pglite.test.ts (existing, not mine). What was still open is closed here: each member's create and issue is one savepoint, so a failure in either rolls both back and no approved award is left un-issued, one member's failure no longer aborts the others' work in the shared transaction, and the run reports failed members (success false) instead of a smaller count. Proved on PostgreSQL: a failed issue leaves no award for that member and the next run completes only that member.

DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-ANNIVERSARY-CR.explanation: The unused years-of-service scale and its helper are removed (credits are the award type's configured amount, which issueAward applies); the years are recorded in the award metadata. The reason text names the organization (read inside the transaction) instead of its UUID, tested on PostgreSQL. No years-of-service credit scale is applied: that would be a product decision on money, not a fix.

DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-SCHEDULED-TASK.explanation: A scheduled rule names an award type and a cron expression but nothing that says who earns the award, so no award can be derived; the task now reports those rules as skipped (and logs a warning) and never as processed. Evaluating scheduled rules remains unbuilt; it is not claimed.

DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-EXPIRATION-TAS.explanation: The durable sent marker needed no new table: the warning is also the member's in-app notice, recorded in in_app_notifications under data.dedupeKey (unique per organization and member, migration 20261103) before the mail leaves; a second run, retry or overlap mails nothing more, and a failed send releases the record so the next run tries again. Proved on PostgreSQL (PGlite) for repeat, retry-after-failure and per-tier behaviour. The mocked notification-service test now mocks the marker (disclosed).
DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-EXPIRATION-TAS.remaining: Nothing in the product sets an expiry or writes an expire entry yet, so the task still has nothing to warn about until an expiry policy is decided and implemented.

DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-AND-WALLET-AND.explanation: The cron lists organizations under system authority and runs each organization's anniversary and scheduled task inside that organization's own RLS context, so the services' shared db handle is subject to row-level security on that path.
DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-AND-WALLET-AND.remaining: The wallet and redemption routes wrapped by withRoleAuth, and the expiration scan (a cross-organization read), still reach the shared handle without a tenant context; each needs its own routing.

DEF-0B11-PRP-REWARDS-CRON-RUNS-ARE-AUDIT.explanation: Each organization's anniversary and scheduled run writes an audit entry (processed, failed or skipped, success) inside its own context, the organizations whose members were e-mailed get an audit entry with the sent and failed counts, an audit that cannot be written fails the run naming the organization, and a member's create and issue are one atomic unit.

DEF-0B9-ORG-ITEM-DELETE-ORGANIZATION-ADM.explanation: The route already refuses an organization's own administrator (403, platform governance required) and gives even a platform administrator no direct archive (501, institutional lifecycle workflow required), so DELETE no longer archives. The source change was upstream's; the regression test proving it (admin refused, non-admin refused, platform admin 501, nothing written, no audit, malformed id 400) is new. The organization aggregate reads now accept both driver result shapes, which also repairs an upstream pglite test that read zero claims.

DEF-0B8-ICRA-CLAIM-TOKEN-HAS-NO-ICRA-ISS.explanation: The paid-tier fulfilment now issues the single-use claim credential (32 random bytes, 30-day expiry, bound to the buyer e-mail) in the same transaction as the tier upgrade, guarded so an existing or consumed credential is never replaced, and a replayed delivery issues nothing.
DEF-0B8-ICRA-CLAIM-TOKEN-HAS-NO-ICRA-ISS.remaining: Nothing delivers the credential to the buyer (the same gap exists for workbooks) and there is no ICRA claim page, so a buyer still cannot present it; delivery needs the e-mail sender and a claim route in the UI.

DEF-0B8-ICRA-REVIEW-DECISION-BY-SHARED-C.explanation: The shared cron secret no longer authorizes a review: the caller must be a signed-in platform administrator (401 / 403 otherwise, nothing written). The reviewer role is the verified governance_reviewer authority; a role asserted in the body is refused unless it matches, and the audit actor is the reviewer's own user id instead of a constant. DEF-0B8-ICRA-CONFIGURE-UPDATE-RESETS-OMI.explanation: An update changes only the fields supplied: sending only a credential reference no longer disables the integration or clears its settings and webhook URL. Switching enabled through configure now carries the same IS NOT DISTINCT FROM concurrency predicate as the activate route (409 and no audit when the state changed), the row is read FOR UPDATE, and the audit records the resulting state, the previous state and which fields changed.

DEF-0B8-JUR-PROFILE-MINIMUM-WAGE-IS-A-PL.explanation: No source of minimum wage rates exists, so none is published: minimumWage is null with minimumWageStatus not_published instead of a zero rate that reads as a real one. Live rates are not provided by this change.

DEF-0B8-JUR-LOCATION-ERASURE-IS-REACHABL.explanation: When there is no active consent to revoke, DELETE now erases whatever location tracking and geofence rows remain (consent expired or already withdrawn, an unfinished retention sweep) and audits the erasure; it answers 404 only when there is neither a consent to revoke nor data to erase, and then keeps no log row. revokeLocationConsent itself is unchanged.

DEF-0B9-ML-SLA-SCORE-IS-LITERAL-WEIGHTS-.explanation: The score is presented as a rule-based heuristic: no confidence, no interval and no training date are returned or stored. Its priority and time remaining are read from the case in the caller's organization (404 for a case that is not), so a caller can no longer choose the inputs that decide an imminent-breach alert; values sent for them are ignored.
DEF-0B9-ML-SLA-SCORE-IS-LITERAL-WEIGHTS-.remaining: The transition count and previous-breach flag are still caller-supplied (they add at most 0.34, so with a case that has time left they cannot reach the 0.80 alert threshold); deriving them needs the claim history.

DEF-0B9-ML-STEWARD-CAN-STORE-ANY-PREDICT.explanation: ml_predictions moves from OPERATIONAL to READ_ONLY in the generic CRUD governance, so the six generic prediction routes can no longer insert or alter a prediction row; only the dedicated scoring routes write it. Covered by the existing governance and route-coverage ratchets.

DEF-0B1-CRUD-FACADE-ORG-MEMBERS.explanation: Every route that was the generic CRUD factory over organization_members under a name that advertises another operation (admin alerts, dues, employment, job classifications, leaves, PKI, roles, segments, system settings, bulk import, member search and others) now answers HTTP 501 behind its original role floor. Only members/[id] still binds the roster table. A contract test fails if another route binds it again. The earlier behaviour (a roster listing presented as the operation, or a refused write) is removed rather than preserved.

DEF-0B2-CRUD-FACADE-SEGMENTS-SETTINGS.explanation: admin/segments, its item and execute routes and admin/system/settings no longer present another table's rows as the operation; they answer 501.

DEF-0B7-PLT-EQUITY-ROUTES-ARE-MEMBER-SEG.explanation: equity/monitoring, self-identify and snapshots answered the generic factory over member_segments. Special-category equity data is neither collected nor monitored there, so they answer 501 and expose no segment rows.

DEF-0B11-IDS-SUPPORT-METRICS-AND-SLA-ROU.explanation: support/metrics and support/sla answered notification rows as support figures; they answer 501.

DEF-0B12-CRUD-SUPPORT-TICKET-PATHS-SERVE.explanation: The ticket collection, item, assign and comments routes answered the same notification rows (assign and comments were the item route); all answer 501.

DEF-0B10-ORG-ROUTES-NAMED-FOR-CARD-CHECK.explanation: The fourteen organizing routes named for assignments, card check, committee, forms, labour board, filings, notes, sequences, support percentage and workplace mapping were campaign-row CRUD. They answer 501 at the officer floor; only organizing/campaigns remains a campaign route.

DEF-0B6-SYS-INHERITANCE-IS-PENDING-PROFI.explanation: continuity/inheritance answered the pre-signup pending_profiles table. It answers 501; the table is no longer bound, so its governance entry was removed (an unlisted table is refused by the fail-closed default). The route test that pinned the old factory configuration was rewritten to pin the 501.

DEF-0B9-ASM-ONBOARDING-TRANSFERS-PATH-IS.explanation: onboarding/transfers re-exported the event recorder behind a guard that always passed; it answers 501. The test that asserted transfers delegated to the audited recorder (and returned 200) was replaced by an assertion that the route answers 501 and does not reuse the recorder.

DEF-0B9-ASM-ONBOARDING-READINESS-IS-THE-.explanation: onboarding/readiness wrapped the pending-profiles handlers behind a placeholder guard; it answers 501.

DEF-0B11-RPT-SHARE-ITEM-PATH-SHARES-NOTH.explanation: reports/[id]/share no longer exposes the report table; its DELETE can no longer remove a report. It answers 501 until a recipient grant exists.

DEF-0B12-CRUD-UPLOAD-PATH-IS-A-JSON-MEDI.explanation: upload answered a JSON insert of a media-library row that receives no file; it answers 501 so a posted file is never reported stored.

DEF-0B6-CMP-INTEGRATIONS-ROUTE-OVER-USER.explanation: enterprise/integrations was the generic factory over oauth_providers (per-user provider ids and tokens, no organization); it answers 501 and the table's governance entry was removed with its last binding.

DEF-0B7-PLT-ENT-EMPTY-200-WITHOUT-ORGANI.explanation: The enterprise integrations path no longer answers an empty 200 for a caller without an organization; it answers 501.

DEF-0B7-PLT-EVENT-OCCURRENCES-PATH-ADDRE.explanation: events/[id]/occurrences was a byte-for-byte copy of the event item route; it answers 501.

DEF-0B6-SYS-CONTINUITY-ALIASES-ARE-THE-D.explanation: The inheritance, archives and docs aliases (the pending-profile table and the document repository behind a guard that always returned true) all answer 501; the document repository itself is reached at /api/documents/repository.

DEF-0B9-ORG-CURRENT-CONTEXT-ROUTE-RETURN.explanation: org/current reads the caller's organization (name, slug, tier, enabled features) under its RLS context and answers 404 when there is no row, instead of a placeholder with a null name.

DEF-0B12-PLT-TENANT-CURRENT-ANSWERS-200-.explanation: tenant/current answers 410 Gone, pointing at org/current. Its old route test (asserting the placeholder body) was deleted and superseded by the 410 test.

DEF-0B12-PLT-QUEUE-STATUS-ANSWERS-AUTHEN.explanation: Access is the service key or a signed-in platform administrator (401 / 403 otherwise); the error text is logged, not returned. The existing queue-status test was adapted to mock the platform-admin guard and logger.

DEF-0B12-PLT-V2-CATCH-ALL-ANSWERS-200-FO.explanation: The catch-all already answers 410 for every method; the source change was upstream's and is covered by an existing test.

DEF-0B12-PLT-V2-CATCH-ALL-ANSWERS-200-WI.explanation: Same: 410 with no data body, upstream's change, existing test.

DEF-0B4-CARBON-FABRICATED-MEASUREMENTS-R.explanation: Carbon routes already answer 501; upstream's change, existing test.

DEF-0B9-ORG-ACCESS-LOGS-ROUTE-IS-ORGANIZ.explanation: The route already answers 501 with no organization row read or written; upstream's change, existing test.

DEF-0B9-ML-SLA-CASE-ID-IS-NEVER-VERIFIED.explanation: Migration 0040 adds ml_predictions.subject_id. The case is verified against the organization (B08) and is now stored on the prediction row, and the audit entry and feedback carry it.

DEF-0B7-COGA-CROSS-DOMAIN-CORRELATIONS-A.explanation: The correlation engine already refuses with NOT_IMPLEMENTED for every organization; the source change was upstream's and is covered by an existing test.

DEF-0B7-COGB-DYNAMICS-ENGINES-EMBED-LITE.explanation: The systems-dynamics, governance-coherence, operational-coordination, operating-rhythm, multi-domain and operational-trust engines embedded fixed frequencies, response times, integration scores and narrative claims (for example "Consistent governance behavior") and presented them as measurements. DEF-0B7-COGB-DYNAMICS-ENGINES-EMBED-LITE.remaining: The response-elasticity and governance-momentum engines remain: they derive scores from counts of cognition-memory entries with arbitrary scaling. They hold no fixed claim, but the scaling is not a validated measure.

DEF-0B7-COGA-ENVELOPE-CONFIDENCE-IS-A-CO.explanation: The default confidence of 60 is gone: an engine states a confidence only when it supplies one (otherwise 0), and the two remaining engines state evidence volume (cognition-memory entries analysed, capped at 100).
DEF-0B7-COGA-ENVELOPE-CONFIDENCE-IS-A-CO.remaining: The explainability envelope's evidence and reasoning lists are still not populated by these engines.

DEF-0B7-EXC-SIMULATION-UNMATCHED-NODES-R.explanation: A scenario that matches no node or role is refused with 400 instead of a canned low-severity result (impact 20, probability 85). DEF-0B7-EXC-SCENARIOS-ALWAYS-RETURN-THE-.explanation: The preset scenarios name roles and no nodes, so every one of them reached the canned minimal result. Roles are now honoured, and a preset that matches nothing in the organization is refused rather than modelled.

DEF-0B7-EXC-SUMMARIZE-STORES-UNVALIDATED.explanation: Model output is validated (non-empty summary, at most five handoff points); anything else is a 502 and nothing is stored. The former fallback text ("Manual review of source content is recommended") that was stored as a generated summary is gone, and its test was replaced.

DEF-0B7-EXC-SUMMARIZE-SENDS-ANY-CONSENT-.explanation: Nothing is sent to the provider unless the retiring employee consented (409 otherwise); interviews above the restricted level go as confidential rather than internal.

DEF-0B7-COGA-CONTINUITY-RISK-SENDS-INTER.explanation: The detector already reads only interviews selected by derivedAnalyticsCondition (published, consented, open levels), proved against real SQL by an existing test; that change was upstream's.

DEF-0B9-ML-CHURN-SCORES-COME-FROM-A-RAND.explanation: The churn route scored members with a randomly initialised network pre-trained on generated examples and stored the score. GET and POST now answer 501 behind the officer floor. The extensive route test, which exercised that scoring with mocks, was replaced by a test of the 501 and of the absence of the generated-example model. Two round-48 ratchet tests that pinned the former handler's organization-input properties (body schema without organizationId, organization-context check) were rewritten to assert that the route now accepts no organization input at all and touches no stored prediction.

DEF-0B9-ML-PREDICTION-ROUTES-ARE-ONE-GEN.explanation: ml/monitoring/drift, monitoring/usage, predictions/claim-outcome, predictions/timeline, predictions/workload-forecast and ml/recommendations were the generic factory over ml_predictions under six model names; all answer 501 and ml_predictions has no generic binding (its governance entry was removed). The monitoring alerts route (GET queried columns and a table that no schema defines and stated a fixed PSI 0.28 drift alert; POST wrote to a table no migration creates) also answers 501; its three POST tests were replaced by one assertion of the 501.

DEF-0B9-ML-OPERATIONAL-METRICS-ARE-PROXI.explanation: The route already reports error_rate as null and no longer names a claim count as a request count; the source change was upstream's and is covered by an existing test.

DEF-0B9-ORG-ANALYTICS-METRIC-QUERIES-RUN.explanation: The member, grievance and growth figures now run under the organization named in the path (its own identity for a direct member, the system role with the exact organization predicate for a platform or parent administrator already authorized), not the caller's own organization, so a federation administrator no longer reads zeros for a local. Average resolution days and the growth rate are null, not 0, when they are undefined. A real-SQL test proves the figures for the officer and for the administrator above. The unit test mocks were adapted to the new call shape (child count first, one members query).

DEF-0B9-ORG-HIERARCHY-ROUTES-PASS-UNVALI.explanation: The children, descendants, ancestors, members and path routes already validate the id (400) and answer 404 for an organization the caller cannot read; the source change was upstream's and is covered by an existing real-SQL test.

DEF-0B10-OPL-03.explanation: POST /api/organizations stores description, province_territory, charter_number and affiliation_date; a value of the wrong shape or an impossible date is refused with 400 rather than dropped under a 201.

DEF-0B10-OPL-08.explanation: The tree read is bounded to the organizations the caller may read, ordered and limited (upstream), and now runs as the system role like the hierarchy route instead of the ambient connection role.

DEF-0B11-RPT-EXECUTE-ROUTE-ALLOWLIST-CHE.explanation: The route kept its own table allowlist, different from the registry the builder and executor use. It now validates against the executor's registry only, so one list governs data sources, fields, filters, joins, having and limits (the executor already resolved and bounded those). The route test mock now uses the real registry.

DEF-0B11-RPT-EXECUTE-FAILURE-IS-ANSWERED.explanation: The executor reports a refused configuration (kind invalid) separately from a failed query (kind failed). DEF-0B11-RPT-DATA-SOURCE-REGISTRY-ADVERT.explanation: The registry named columns the tables do not have (claims.outcome, members first_name/last_name, deadlines current_deadline) and a joinable table that is not a source (claim_notes). They now map to the physical columns (resolution_outcome, due_date), the member name is the single field name, and a new ratchet fails if a registry column is not a physical column of its table. A saved report that named first_name or last_name is refused rather than run against a missing column.

DEF-0B11-SOC-INTERNAL-SIGNATURE-PROVIDER.explanation: The built-in provider generated envelope ids and sign URLs, stored and sent nothing, and reported every envelope as sent. It is removed: the default provider is a configured DocuSign or HelloSign account or a 501, and the document route refuses any other provider name. The tests of the stub were removed and replaced by tests that there is no built-in provider and no stub fallback.
DEF-0B11-SOC-INTERNAL-SIGNATURE-PROVIDER.remaining: Documents already stored with provider "internal" keep that value; their status sync reports provider_unavailable and their void is attempted against no provider.

DEF-0B11-SOC-ANALYTICS-AND-ENGAGEMENT-FI.explanation: Existing collection-unavailable and data_collected safeguards remain. Additionally, the post analytics summary, campaign analytics summary and campaign export no longer claim zero clicks when no click collector or click field exists; they return null (unknown) while account analytics retains actual recorded linkClicks. Regression assertions cover all three projections; tests and native/runtime acceptance remain pending.
DEF-0B11-SOC-ANALYTICS-AND-ENGAGEMENT-FI.remaining: The social platform collector still does not transform provider responses into stored analytics and no proven worker calls it. Exact-HEAD unit, native PostgreSQL and HTTP/browser/staging qualification and institutional analytics authority remain outstanding.

DEF-0B11-IDS-STEWARD-ROUTES-SERVE-ASSIGN.explanation: The directory route is a member-safe projection for members, full rows (audited) for officers, and answers 405 to writes; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

DEF-0B11-IDS-SATISFACTION-REPRESENTATIVE.explanation: A representative with no completed surveys, or an unknown id, is a 404 rather than 200 with zero averages; a caller with no organization is refused rather than reading across organizations.

DEF-0B11-IDS-SATISFACTION-CREATE-DOES-NO.explanation: A survey can only be created for a resolved or closed claim (409 otherwise), and a claim with no assigned representative is refused (400) instead of accepting any representative id. The existing test fixtures were given a claim status and extended with the new refusals.

DEF-0B11-IDS-SETTINGS-PUT-IS-UNVALIDATED.explanation: name (1-200), shortName (at most 50) and provinceTerritory (at most 100) are validated before anything is read; a missing body or organization is a 400, not a server error. The settings merge reads the row under FOR UPDATE and writes in the same transaction, and a missing row is a 404 with no audit.

DEF-0B3-EXTERNAL-INVOICES-WRITE-ADVERTIS.explanation: The invoice create path answers 501 stating that invoices are ingested from the provider; the contract test pins that it never inserts.

DEF-0B3-SEND-INVOICE-NOT-SENT.explanation: The route generated a platform invoice and delivered nothing. It answers 501 behind the steward floor (generation remains POST /api/finance/invoices and the billing batch). Its test, which asserted the generation, was replaced by an assertion of the 501 and of the absence of the generator.

DEF-0B4-CBA-EXPORT-SILENTLY-TRUNCATED.explanation: The export asked for 10000 rows but the list serves at most 100 a page, so the file silently held the first page. It reads every page and refuses (400) a result set over 10000, naming the count, instead of cutting it.

DEF-0B4-CLAUSE-LIBRARY-COMPARE-GET-STUB-.explanation: The GET stub (a 200 with a usage hint) is removed (405). commonKeywords is now computed from the compared clause texts (words of four letters or more, not stop words, present in every clause, ranked by frequency; English and French). Clause ids are validated as ids and a malformed body is a 400. The route test fixtures use real ids now.

DEF-0B5-COMMITTEE-INTELLIGENCE-PLACEHOLD.explanation: POST stored a snapshot whose summary said synthesis was pending and whose themes, positions and recommendations were empty. It checks authority and then answers 501; nothing is stored. The snapshot list is unchanged.

DEF-0B6-CMP-FIREWALL-POLICY-NO-WRITER-OR.explanation: The route served a table no route writes and nothing enforces under the name of an employer data firewall. It answers 501 and the table's governance entry was removed. The writeRole test for the route was rewritten to assert the 501 and the absence of the table binding, and the committed schema mutation program was regenerated because the table is now unreachable from any route.

DEF-0B6-CMP-DISPATCH-RULES-ENGINE-NEVER-.explanation: An assignment accepted any member ids for a request in any state, in any number, with no check that they were members, and counted the request filled from the ids of one call. It now requires an open or partly filled request of the caller's organization (row locked), active members of that organization, no worker already offered or placed, and no more offers than workers requested, with a distinct status for each refusal. Proven on real SQL. Three mock-chain tests of assignWorkersToDispatch were removed because the mocks cannot express these queries; the pglite suite replaces them.
DEF-0B6-CMP-DISPATCH-RULES-ENGINE-NEVER-.remaining: rankCandidates still scores a candidate list nothing supplies (no source of member skills or availability), and the assignment is an officer's explicit selection, not engine-ranked.

DEF-0B6-CMP-DASHBOARD-STATS-FAILURE-RETU.explanation: A failed query is an error and the member count is null for an ordinary member, not zero; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

DEF-0B6-CMP-EXPORT-CSV-AUTHENTICATION-ON.explanation: The export answers 501 in every environment; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

DEF-0B8-ICRA-PAID-PDF-REPORT-GATE-REQUIR.explanation: The report gate accepts submitted as well as completed, so a paid report is no longer refused for a status nothing writes; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

DEF-0B8-ICRA-CHECKOUT-SELLS-A-TIER-WITHO.explanation: Checkout now reads the assessment status and answers 409 with no Stripe session unless the assessment is submitted or completed, so a buyer is never charged for a report the report route would refuse.

DEF-0B8-ICRA-INTEGRATION-CREDENTIALS-NEV.explanation: The public configuration no longer reports credentialsStored: true for every integration: it reports false, with credentialsResolvable false, because only a reference is held.
DEF-0B8-ICRA-INTEGRATION-CREDENTIALS-NEV.remaining: A credentialRef is still accepted and stored and nothing resolves it to a secret; a vault-backed resolution path does not exist.

DEF-0B9-ASM-FEDERATION-MATCH-IGNORES-THE.explanation: The sector now scores (25, case-insensitive match against the federation's sectors) and "Similar size" is stated only when the smaller count is at least half the larger. The reason text "Similar size category", which was given for any ratio, is gone and its test was changed to the new text.

DEF-0B9-ASM-SMART-DEFAULTS-ARE-A-LITERAL.explanation: The route served a literal table of features, integrations and limits by organization type that nothing defines or applies. It answers 501; its test of the table was replaced by an assertion of the 501.

DEF-0B11-PRP-RECONCILIATION-RUNS-ARE-NOT.explanation: For an organization run, the period is locked, a billing period named in the request must be the organization's own (404), and a second run for the same period is refused (409, naming the earlier run) instead of adding a second set of exceptions. A period that ends before it starts is refused. The existing mocked test of a run gained the two new checks in its queue; three tests were added.
DEF-0B11-PRP-RECONCILIATION-RUNS-ARE-NOT.remaining: The service still accepts a run with no organization, which reconciles every organization together; no route uses that mode, but it is not removed.

DEF-0B12-CRUD-TESTIMONIAL-APPROVAL-COMPO.explanation: The component sent status, reviewedAt, reviewedBy, rejectionReason and isFeatured; the table has approvedAt and featured only. It now sends those, the route stamps the approval with the server clock once, and the reject flow is removed because the table cannot record a rejection (the component has no importer).

DEF-0B12-PLT-VOCABULARY-SERVES-UNSOURCED.explanation: The six vocabulary routes serve identifiers, labels, descriptions and categories only. Service-level hours, escalation, legal and settlement flags, role permissions, default priority and severity, and status transitions are no longer served as institutional reference data; the case state machine still reads them from the package server-side.

DEF-0B4-CBA-INTEL-TENANT-ADMIN-WRITES-SH.explanation: The extracted CBA dataset (agreements, findings, wage adjustments, clauses, sources, ingestion) has no organization column. A contract test checks all seven mutating handlers. The extraction route test gained the platform-admin mock and a refusal test.

DEF-0B4-CBA-INTEL-TENANT-STEWARD-REVIEWS.explanation: The review queue and review decisions (approve, reject, supersede) changed rows every organization reads at the steward floor of any one organization. Both methods now require a platform administrator and the reviewer role recorded is platform_administrator, not a literal "steward". A refusal test covers the queue and the decision, which write and read nothing.

DEF-0B4-CBA-INTEL-SHARED-DATASET-NO-TENA.explanation: Writes and review are now platform authority. The dataset is shared by design (no organization column), so a tenant predicate does not apply to its reads.
DEF-0B4-CBA-INTEL-SHARED-DATASET-NO-TENA.remaining: Reads (agreements list and detail, benchmark, documents, freshness) remain open to any entitled member or steward of any organization; whether the shared dataset may be read that widely, and under which entitlement, is an institutional decision.

DEF-0B3-ARBITRATION-DECISIONS-ORG-ADMIN-.explanation: The collection and item routes already require the platform content_manager role to write; upstream's change, now pinned by a contract test.

DEF-0B4-CASE-STUDIES-ORG-ADMIN-WRITES-GL.explanation: Case-study writes need content_manager and the item route (read and write) is limited to it; upstream's change, pinned by a contract test.

DEF-0B4-CASE-STUDIES-READ-IGNORES-PUBLIC.explanation: The public list is limited to public, already published rows for both the rows and the count, and a status other than published is refused; upstream's change, pinned by a contract test.

DEF-0B3-BARGAINING-PROPOSALS-NO-TENANT-P.explanation: Proposals are scoped through their negotiation (parentScope), because the table has no organization column; upstream's change, pinned by a contract test.

DEF-0B9-ASM-PEER-BENCHMARKS-AND-CLAUSE-S.explanation: Both routes compare or suggest for the caller's own organization. DEF-0B9-ORG-ROSTER-GET-INCLUDES-REMOVED-.explanation: The roster excludes removed members and is read a page at a time (default and maximum 200) in a stable order; proven on real SQL, including that consecutive pages do not overlap.

DEF-0B11-IDS-SCIM-LIST-INCLUDES-REMOVED-.explanation: The SCIM list excludes removed members, counts and pages in SQL from the requested start index, and no longer loads the whole roster.

DEF-0B11-IDS-SCIM-PROVISION-STORES-THE-U.explanation: Provisioning creates a pending membership, not an active one, so naming a user grants no access until the person accepts.

DEF-0B11-IDS-SATISFACTION-PENDING-LIST-H.explanation: The pending list is bound to the caller's organization as well as the member; the route refuses a caller with no organization.

DEF-0B8-HS-TRENDS-ORGANIZATION-FROM-QUER.explanation: The trends read the authenticated organization only, as predicate and RLS binding; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

DEF-0B9-ML-CHURN-RESOLVES-A-SECOND-IDENT.explanation: The churn route answers 501 and reads no claims (batch B10), so its second identity resolution and unscoped claim read no longer exist.

DEF-0B9-ML-ALERTS-ACKNOWLEDGEMENT-JOIN-H.explanation: The alerts route answers 501 and reads nothing (batch B10).

DEF-0B9-ASM-FEDERATION-DISCOVERY-LISTS-F.remaining: It remains a directory of federations by name and member count, readable by any organization's officer; whether that directory may be shown to every organization is an institutional decision.

DEF-0B4-CLAUSES-SEARCH-FACADE.explanation: clauses/search listed the clause table without searching; it answers 501.

DEF-0B9-ORG-ANALYTICS-ANY-SIGNED-IN-USER.explanation: The analytics route answers 404 to a caller with no read authority over the organization named in the path and is officer-level for those who have it (batch B11 and upstream, existing tests including real SQL).

DEF-0B6-CMP-CONTRACT-CREATE-REFERENCES-U.explanation: A contract create checks that its billing account and subscription belong to the caller's organization (400 malformed, 404 otherwise) before anything is written; a contract provisions entitlements from its lines.

DEF-0B6-EMP-TIMESHEET-INGEST-STEWARD-FLO.explanation: The list is officer-level and bounded to 200 batches; a new batch needs calendar dates in order, a file name of at most 255 characters and a CSV of at most 2,000,000 characters. DEF-0B6-EMP-TIMESHEET-INGEST-STEWARD-FLO.remaining: The ingest still sits at the steward floor rather than a financial mandate, and no behavioural test of the route exists (contract test only).

DEF-0B7-EXC-SEARCH-LIMITS-BEFORE-FILTERI.explanation: The keyword search puts the sensitivity floor in the query so the limit counts only readable interviews, treats LIKE wildcards in the query as literals, and reads nothing when no level is allowed. Test disclosure: the drizzle mock gained inArray and one test was added.

DEF-0B10-PEN-TRUSTEE-MEETING-READS-RETUR.explanation: List and item reads are restricted to the pension financial administrator role, bound to the tenant, paginated and audited (upstream's change, existing test). This is an engineering restriction, not an issued trustee mandate.

DEF-0B10-PEN-TRUSTEE-MEETING-MINUTES-CAN.explanation: Amendment and deletion of trustee meetings are refused until a versioned amendment and retention workflow exists (upstream's change, existing test).

DEF-0B10-PEN-T4A-POST-STORES-AN-ADMINIST.explanation: T4A generation answers 501 and stores nothing (upstream's change, existing test).

DEF-0B10-PEN-PLAN-DELETE-REMOVES-THE-PLA.explanation: DELETE now terminates the plan (status and time) and keeps the row and its enrolments, contributions and claims; a repeat is 409 and a foreign plan 404, audited in the same transaction. Test disclosure: the route had no test, so none was replaced.

DEF-0B12-PLT-VOICE-TRANSCRIBE-HAS-NO-RAT.explanation: Transcription is rate limited per caller, requires an organization context, and records the disclosure (language, size, type; never the audio or text) before the recording leaves; if the audit cannot be written nothing is sent.
DEF-0B12-PLT-VOICE-TRANSCRIBE-HAS-NO-RAT.remaining: There is no entitlement or consent decision for sending a recording to the external service.

DEF-0B12-WBK-MEMORY-HOLDER-ROUTES-ACCEPT.explanation: The collection reads and writes run through the public-intake guard (rate limit; body cap on writes). Claimed-workbook writes were already audited.
DEF-0B12-WBK-MEMORY-HOLDER-ROUTES-ACCEPT.remaining: The per-holder item route is not yet behind the guard, there is no per-workbook holder cap, and unclaimed-workbook reads are not audited.

DEF-0B5-COMMS-SUBSCRIBER-EMAILS-READ-BY-.explanation: Distribution lists and their subscriber e-mail addresses are read at the steward floor, and the subscriber list is bounded to 5000 rows. Test disclosure: the subscribers route test's mock chain gained limit.

DEF-0B7-PLT-EXT-PATCH-STEWARD-FLOOR-REWR.explanation: Rewriting an integration's endpoint and field mapping needs an administrator, as the delete already did.

DEF-0B6-CMP-CONTRACT-AUDIT-NOT-ATOMIC.explanation: Contract create, activate and terminate write their audit record in the same transaction (persistAtomicAudit) instead of a separate best-effort logger call. Test disclosure: the service test now mocks persistAtomicAudit in place of the logger.

DEF-0B8-JUR-KNOWLEDGE-BASE-ITEM-GET-INCR.explanation: The system-context counter update names the organization of the row that was read.

DEF-0B6-CMP-VALIDATE-ATTESTS-FROM-CALLER.explanation: The strike-vote and certification checks no longer return compliant, warning or violation from numbers the caller typed against thresholds written into the route; each reports the arithmetic, says no validated rule is configured and that the figures are unchecked, as info. Test disclosure: one test added; the existing tests did not assert a verdict.

DEF-0B6-CMP-VALIDATE-LITERAL-THRESHOLDS-.explanation: The literal thresholds are removed and there is no rule lookup to swallow.

DEF-0B8-JUR-COMPLIANCE-CHECK-REPORTS-ZER.explanation: The response carries the number of checks evaluated and, when none applied, a notice that this is not a finding of compliance.

DEF-0B6-CMP-AUDIT-LOG-FULL-ROW-READ-BY-O.explanation: The organization audit-log list names eight columns (who, what, which resource, severity, outcome, time) and no longer serves the captured old and new values, network address, user agent, session and correlation ids, metadata, error text or archive path. The read is still audited in the same transaction.

DEF-0B6-CMP-AUDIT-MANUAL-ENTRY-FREE-REFE.explanation: A manual entry is recorded as compliance.manual_entry attributed to the administrator who wrote it, with the declared fields kept as untrusted details, so it cannot pass for a system record (upstream's change, existing test).

DEF-0B5-COMMS-CAMPAIGN-STATUS-AND-STATS-.explanation: A campaign create accepts author fields only, and a PATCH blocks status, send times, delivery statistics and the audience count; campaigns are read at the steward floor because they carry segment queries and bodies.

DEF-0B5-SURVEY-LIFECYCLE-WRITABLE-DIRECT.explanation: A survey moves draft, then active or published, then closed, never backwards; the server stamps the publication time once; response counts, views and completion are never client-written and a new survey cannot be created already published.

DEF-0B5-POLLS-ITEM-ROUTE-IS-COLLECTION.explanation: The poll item route was mounting the collection handlers (GET and POST), so no poll could be read, changed or removed by id; it is now an item route on [pollId] with the same lifecycle guard, and the vote totals are blocked from PATCH.

DEF-0B1-VERSION-UNAUTH-TOPOLOGY.explanation: Anonymous callers receive only the build identity; the environment, host, deployment type, feature profile and image digests need the deployment-probe credential, always with no-store (upstream's change, existing test).

DEF-0B6-EMP-REPLAY-NOT-IDEMPOTENT-GATES-.explanation: A replay identical in run, mode, rule version, engine version and result is answered with the replay already made, adding no replay row, artifacts, evidence link, compliance event or audit duplicate; a different requested mode is a new replay. DEF-0B11-PRP-PRECEDENT-SEARCH-USES-UNESC.explanation: Search terms take the LIKE wildcards literally, the search accepts only the two filters it reads (strict, bounded lists), and a filter value outside the column's declared values is refused with 400 instead of reaching the database as a 500.
